physical_harm: Two persons died due to gunshot injuries
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation/planning as an act of retaliation and vengeance
motive: Retaliation and vengeance due to rejection of marriage proposal
key_evidence_accepted: The dying declaration of the victim 'KV' and the statements of her relations, who had appeared as prosecution witnesses, duly established the commission of the offence, as well as, the common motive for the two accused to have joined hands in committing the crime.
witness_credibility: The three eye-witnesses, a young boy, the wife of the deceased and an old grandmother were natural witnesses, whose presence at the place of occurrence, did not cast any shadow of doubt.
trial_duration: The occurrence took place at 10:30 hrs. on 28.7.2003. The trial court convicted the appellants on 30.12.2005. The High Court affirmed the order on 2.9.2009. The Supreme Court judgment was delivered on 11.10.2011.
legal_representation: R.N. Mittal, Arvind Kumar Gupta, Rahul Mangla and Mohit Garg for the Appellant. Naresh K. Sharma for the Respondent.
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution established that the accused committed the offence as an act of retaliation and vengeance due to the rejection of a marriage proposal. The dying declaration of the victim and the statements of her relations, along with the evidence of the eye-witnesses, established the commission of the offence and the common motive for the two accused to have joined hands in committing the crime.
defence_argument: The accused no.2 pleaded that he had no role in the crime, as all the shots were fired by accused no.1 and he was merely a bystander. The appellants also argued that the case was fabricated and that the family of the deceased remained quiet until the disclosure of the names of the offenders.
legal_principle_applied: Proof of motive is not a sine qua non before a person can be held guilty of the commission of a crime. Motive being a matter of the mind, is more often than not, difficult to establish through evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Uttar Pradesh vs. Sahrunnisa & Anr. (2009) 15 SCC 452; Aizaz & Others vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2008) 12 SCC 198; State of Uttar Pradesh v. Rajvir (2007) 15 SCC 545
